messages:
Maya R.: spinning up a small canary for the new p95 SLO token-sculptor. seeing a weird tail on /generate-chat-leftover, logs below

Omar K.: can you paste the profiler snippet and kernel selection? which routes hit it?

Maya R.: quick profiler excerpt:
```
kernel_selected: attn_fused_fast
avg_time_per_token: 0.95ms
p95_time_per_token: 1.6ms
batch_size_distribution: 1,1,2,3,6,8,12 (median 4)
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.62 (down from 0.88 baseline)
queue_policy: p95-led-token-allocator
route: /generate-chat-leftover (tier: medium, interactive=true)
```

perf-bot: perf-alert: route=/generate-chat-leftover p95 +120ms vs baseline (recent canary) :warning:

Liam P.: sounds like token budget is too permissive for medium tier -> lots of tiny microbatches, prefetch thrash + cache churn. seen similar with `aggressive_token` profiles.

Jen S.: KV hit-rate drop to ~62% when prefix caching was effectively bypassed in canary config (we disabled persistent prefix cache for test). any kernel changes that could explain CPU/GPU time?

Omar K.: no global kernel swap for A100 path. we did flip fallback kernel to `attn_v2_fused` for V100 fallback group last week; that kernel costs about +0.8ms/token for long context (seq>512). might amplify p95 when cache misses force longer prefixes.

Maya R.: current experiment config:
```
batcher:
  token_budget_by_tier:
    high: 400
    medium: 256
    low: 120
  queue_policy: p95-led-token-allocator
  prefetch: true
  kv_prefetch_window: 32
  kernel_fallback_threshold: 1.0
canary:
  nodes: 2
  traffic: 3%
  region: us-west2
```

Liam P.: when we switch `queue_policy` to fair-shared, tail improves but throughput takes a hit. p95-led keeps latency SLO for high-tier but starves medium with tiny batches. my thinking: lower medium token_budget and enable adaptive prefetching.

Jen S.: proposal: medium token_budget 256 -> 180, kv_prefetch=auto, set kernel_fallback_threshold=1.2 to avoid switching to slower fused kernel unless necessary. also enable prefix sticky caching for 5m TTL.

Omar K.: @infra-bot can you spin canary nodes on V100 fleet (us-west2) to replicate the kernel fallback path? want identical HW to the impacted pods.

infra-bot: scheduled canary: 2 nodes (v100), window 30m, traffic 3%, note=replicate kernel fallback path

Maya R.: starting canary now with Jen's config tweaks. will repost p95 snapshots at +15m. :rocket:

perf-bot: canary snapshot (@15m): baseline p95=210ms, canary p95=185ms, kv_hit=0.82, median=98ms. improvement concentrated on routes with prefix reuse.

Maya R.: looks promising. immediate win from kv_prefetch=auto and reducing medium budget. next step: run a 2h canary at 10% and monitor regression windows. will also add a microprofiler probe around kernel selection to catch unexpected fallbacks.

Omar K.: sg. I'll add logging for kernel_fallback_reason and a metric for "prefetch_evictions_per_min".

Jen S.: if sustained, plan rollout: medium budget -> 160, enable prefix sticky cache by default for interactive routes, keep kernel_fallback_threshold=1.2. create a short postmortem writeup if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

Maya R.: thanks team — will follow up with graphs and canary link in ~45m.
